title: ShopMind — visual world, round 2
question: The reroll assigned the Appliance Rating Plate. Keep it, take the resistor-code pick or a challenger, go category standard, or re-roll again.

options.label: Rating Plate
options.lineage: the riveted nameplate on every manufactured appliance — stamped specs, serials, cert seals
options.thesis: Every product, order, and quote is an appliance wearing its factory plate: stamped name, engraved spec table, riveted corners.
options.viewport: A brushed-aluminum masthead rail with riveted wordmark; the catalog as a wall of nameplates — each card a stamped product name over an engraved spec table with serial, stock, and price; blue ink marks agent annotations, safety yellow appears only on controls a human can press; cert seals stamp status (RESERVED, PAID, EXPIRED).
options.risk: If the plates stop being data-dense and become decorative metal, it turns into skeuomorphic costume.

raised.raise: Duration reads from geometry: the quote-expiry seal is a dial whose remaining arc is the remaining minutes.
One dominant color region per work area: admin panels own a committed hue zone, not uniform gray.

options.label: Resistor Code
options.lineage: electronics workbench color-code system, IEERC 62 band values
options.thesis: The store speaks in band codes: categories, prices, and stock carry a color-band encoding every engineer can read.
options.viewport: Parts-bin drawer rail on the left; products as component labels with 4-band chips encoding category + stock; filters are band sequences you compose; price tabular, tolerance marks on deals.
options.risk: The encoding is real but only legible once learned — new demo visitors need the legend before the language works.

options.label: Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: segmented boarding pass paired with a live flight-status board
options.thesis: The quote is a perforated pass; order status is a gate board where a changed row reranks in place and stays lit.
options.viewport: Checkout summary as a segmented pass with a scannable block; orders desk as a gate board sorted by time; alert color fires only on state changes.
options.case: Holds the clarity axis outright — rerank-and-stay-lit is exactly how order status should behave; loses audience-nativism because it is a travel world, not electronics.
options.risk: A pass-shaped checkout reads as costume once the flight metaphor is dropped.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.lineage: Windows Phone Metro — flat tiles, giant lowercase, zero chrome
options.thesis: Products as live tiles that flip to show fresh data; type is the interface, borders are deleted.
options.viewport: Catalog as a tile grid where stock/price tiles flip; nav is a horizontal panorama of panes; chromeless.
options.case: Holds audience identification — every reviewer of a certain age typed this on a phone; loses clarity because panorama sliding fights cart/checkout wayfinding.
options.risk: Near-black + neon-ish accents is a calibration rut unless the tile discipline stays strict.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Catalog entries in strict number sequence; labels encoded as hue strips.
options.viewport: Dealt again this roll — same hand as round one, full anatomy in its earlier sketch.
options.case: Holds audience identification for design-literate engineers; loses product clarity because encoded labels hide meaning behind hover.
options.risk: You already saw and passed this exact card last round.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.lineage: dance notation — shape is direction, length is duration
options.case: Loses both axes: dancers know it, engineers don’t; a mirrored vertical staff under a product grid is costume.
options.kept: Duration you can measure with a ruler — now a named raise: the expiry seal’s remaining arc is the remaining time.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: zoo & garden guide maps — flat lobes, capsule pins
options.case: Loses both axes on an operating surface: visitors don’t map-identify, and lobe geometry can’t carry a working catalog.
options.kept: One dominant color region per screen — now a named raise for the assigned direction’s work areas.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The expected electronics storefront, executed at impeccable craft.
canonCard.viewport: Filter rail, product cards, cart drawer, assistant panel — pure convention at full polish.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every competitor by design.
